gaps.sentence: I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)

gaps.sentence: Despite ___ three times, he didn't give up.
We managed ___ everyone before the storm hit.
She made her son ___ his room before dinner.
gaps.explanation: make + object + bare infinitive: made him tidy (passive takes to: was made to tidy).

gaps.sentence: They've postponed ___ the new bridge until spring.
This new timetable will mean ___ earlier trains.
After introducing herself, she went on ___ the main findings.
gaps.hint: move on to a new activity
gaps.explanation: go on + to-infinitive = do something after finishing something else.

gaps.sentence: We stopped ___ something to eat at the motorway services.
gaps.explanation: 'Stopped to get' = paused for the purpose; 'stopped getting' would mean quit eating.
